scope: Versioned and replayable agent evaluation workflows
does_not_establish: A bounded inspiration artifact, not a research-gap, novelty, prevalence, or lifecycle certificate.

sources.title: AgentBeats: Agentifying Agent Assessment for Openness, Standardization, and Reproducibility

inspection_spans.observation: AgentBeats separates judge and subject agents through standardized protocols and treats benchmark administration as an explicit workflow.
A standardized pipeline preserves broad fidelity while enabling cross-agent comparisons.
Harness-swapping changes solve rates and token use; native model-harness pairings are not interchangeable.

sources.supports: Evidence that agent, harness, benchmark, and protocol are separable evaluation components and harness choice changes outcomes.
sources.does_not_establish: Causal attribution for arbitrary deployments or reproducibility from openness alone.

sources.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures

inspection_spans.observation: CAR distinguishes the step executing harm from the earlier decision step and uses same-policy interventions rather than transcript judgment.
The paper narrows its contribution relative to oracle substitution and static-log attribution.
Real side-effecting tools are out of scope, mocked reproducible tools are used, judges add noise, and the validation ground truth is synthetic.

sources.supports: A counterfactual attribution instrument and a point-of-commitment distinction.
sources.does_not_establish: Faithful replay of live side-effecting tools or a field-level causal attribution result.

sources.title: AgentLab reproducibility documentation

inspection_spans.observation: Reproducibility changes with software versions, silently updated API models, live websites, region/language defaults, stochastic agents, and nondeterministic tasks; studies record versions and commits.
AgentXray can inspect actions in previous or ongoing experiments but warns that its own display layer can behave unexpectedly.

sources.supports: A concrete benchmark workflow showing that public assets alone do not freeze software, providers, environments, regional language, or inspection tooling.
sources.does_not_establish: The size of each effect or a universal replay contract.

sources.title: ClawBench/ShellBench reproducibility-first benchmark release

inspection_spans.observation: The release versions its diagnostics and explicitly scores the full stack—harness, configuration, and model—rather than only the LLM.
Long-horizon and human-baseline coverage are planned rather than present in Core v1.

sources.supports: An operational full-stack evaluation posture and explicit versioned coverage limits.
sources.does_not_establish: Scientific validation of its diagnostics, broad human calibration, or causal attribution.

tension_clusters.label: Agent scores are reported as model capability while software, harness, provider, website, region/language, configuration, and judge remain moving parts
tension_clusters.actor: Agent benchmark maintainers and model/system selectors
tension_clusters.incumbent_practice: Publish open code/assets and compare aggregate scores under a nominal benchmark name.
tension_clusters.material_consequence: Teams may attribute a score change to the agent and choose or remediate the wrong component when the execution contract drifted.
alternative_explanations: Observed replay differences are judge noise or stochastic continuation
tension_clusters.does_not_establish: A universal replay mechanism, causal attribution for live tools, or that openness guarantees reproducibility.

controller_boundary: Review-only source reduction; no gap, novelty, prevalence, proposal, or lifecycle transition is established.
